title: Genera → Ramp deployment configuration (desired state)
description: The desired-state configuration your pipeline produces for one customer. Field shapes intentionally mirror Ramp's Developer API create-request bodies where an API exists (see docs.ramp.com). Where no API exists to apply a section, the section still belongs here as desired state — and the gap belongs in your audit log.

base_currency.description: ISO 4217 code all normalized amounts are stated in, e.g. USD

entities.description: Legal entities spend is organized under. NOTE: check what the Ramp API lets you do with entities before assuming your pipeline can create them.

status.description: existing = already present in the customer's Ramp instance; requested = customer wants it created

entity.description: entities[].name this department belongs to, if stated

role.description: Ramp invitable role. If a source document asks for a role outside this enum, that's a mapping decision — record it.

direct_manager_email.description: null if unknown — and if unknown, say so in the audit log

spend_programs.description: Reusable spend templates (e.g. Software, Travel, Field Ops). Mirrors POST /spend-programs.

limits.description: Per-person or per-team spend limits (the objects cards draw from). Mirrors the Limits API create body.

assigned_to.description: Exactly one of user_email or group must be set.

group.description: a department name or a named cohort, e.g. 'Field Reps'

spend_program.description: spend_programs[].display_name this limit is issued from, if any

approval_policies.description: Approval chains as desired state. Before assuming your pipeline can apply these, check what the Ramp API supports — and record what you find.

applies_to.description: what spend this policy governs (a department, spend program, or 'all')

threshold_usd_cents.description: amounts at or above this require this approver; 0 = auto-approve tier

approver.description: AUTO, DIRECT_MANAGER, or a role/person, e.g. 'VP Finance (dmarsh@acme.example)'

source.description: which document/line this policy came from — matters when sources conflict

mcc_controls.description: Category controls, stated the way Ramp can enforce them. Note carefully which direction (allow vs block) and which vocabulary (Ramp category codes vs raw MCC codes) the API actually accepts.

mechanism.description: the actual API field you would use

translation_notes.description: how you got from what the customer said to this mechanism — e.g. MCC allowlist → category allowlist mapping

limit_amount_cents.description: smallest currency unit, per Ramp convention

currency.description: ISO 4217. If you normalized from another currency, record the source amount and rate in the audit log.

lock_date.description: ISO 8601 date to auto-lock (useful for temporary cards)
